paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Taanit, chapter 2, halakhah 4, and in the Pesikta cited as דר״ב, 154a, speaking in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. The statement is cited in Vayikra Rabbah 29:9, and there: Rav Bivi bar Abba in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.

notes.text: The supplied Pesikta designation is דר״ב. Pesikta deRav Kahana is the draft’s proposed identification, but the abbreviation and historical 154a reference remain unverified here. ר״י in the final clause follows the immediately preceding full Yochanan name; the Pesikta identity remains open.

Midrash Rabbah -- TE Vayikra Rabbah 29:9 independently confirms the report in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, with the form Rabbi Bivi bar Abba (רבי ביבי בר אבא). Hyman’s supplied Rav and the heading Biva Rabbah remain distinct source forms. This comparison does not identify Pesikta דר״ב or verify 154a.

Buber’s Lyck edition of Pesikta deRav Kahana, 154a and its continuation, confirms Biva Rabbah quoting Rabbi Yochanan in Abraham’s prayer about the binding of Isaac. Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:4 has Rabbi Bibi Abba (Guggenheimer’s note gives “the Elder Rabbi Bevai” in G). The consulted Hebrew of Vayikra Rabbah 29:9 has Rabbi Bibi bar Abba, while its English reads “bar Abaye.” These are distinct readings of the attribution.
